findings.where: First screen at desktop: the 'Write to me' margin note in the left gutter
findings.fault: The page's one action is the weakest thing in the first screen. Squinting, the 64 px heading wins, then the dark photo stand-in, then the aqueduct sketch, and the note comes fourth. It is a small script line out in the margin. It lines up with no line of the hero copy: it sits below the italic experience line and level with the top of the sketch, so by proximity it belongs to neither the text group nor the drawing.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer scanning the first screen for how to reach Mark reads the heading, sees the photo and drawing, and has to search the far-left edge to find a small red scribble. Mark wants that contact to happen.

findings.where: Article specimen: the closing rule under the PDF link row ('Streamlining the PPP Process…' / 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'), at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The row's bottom rule is drawn at the height of a one-line row, but both cells wrap to two lines (three on phone). The rule runs through the bottom of '‘Abundance’ Challenge' and '2026 · PDF', so the text looks struck through or crammed against its own border.
findings.who_objects: A reader going down Mark's article list sees a broken, cramped row, which hurts the careful-lawyer impression. Angélique will see it on every post or PDF entry whose title wraps.

findings.where: Article specimen at desktop: the heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' and the handwritten pull quote ('whichever PPP Law…'), and the pull quote again at phone
findings.fault: Snapping to the 32 px rules leaves a two-rule (64 px) line pitch on type much smaller than that. The heading's two lines, and the quote's lines, sit as far apart as separate paragraphs. On phone the quote stretches to four widely spaced lines, so neither reads as one block (proximity). The hero heading, set at its full 64 px, does not have this problem, so the article page's rhythm is looser than the homepage's.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles reads a broken heading and a quote that falls apart line by line. Since the article page is where the Read mode lives, this weakens the template Angélique will fill with every post.

findings.where: First screen at desktop: the aqueduct sketch below the hero copy
findings.fault: The sketch is centred on the page (about 518–1055 px). It straddles the gap between the text column (256–859) and the photo column (891–1311), so it continues neither column's edge. It reads as a separate object dropped between the hero and the palette, not as part of either.
findings.who_objects: Mark, judging whether the drawing looks sketched straight onto his pad. A drawing that lines up with nothing looks placed, not drafted.

findings.where: Palette swatches, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: Each swatch's three caption lines (name, hex, role) are spaced out on the 32 px rules. The last line ends about as close to the swatch below as the name is to its own swatch, so by proximity the captions hang between rows rather than under their own colour.
findings.who_objects: Mark, or the next round's designer, reading the tile has to work out which hex and role belong to which chip.

findings.fault: The second row of links spreads from edge to edge (16–374 px) and the mark sits at 16 px. The page content starts at 56 px, right of the margin line, so the bar and the page share no left edge. On desktop the mark lines up with the margin line.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor sees a top bar that doesn't line up with the page under it. It is a small loss of the tidy, ruled-pad order the direction promises.
